Photograph: Andy Rain/EPAGraeme WeardenTue 20 Oct 2026 07.22 BSTFirst published on Tue 20 Oct 2026 07.15 BSTShareFrom 6m ago07.15 BSTIntroduction: UK unemployment rate falls in pre-budget boost
Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets and the world economy.
The UK unemployment rate has fallen, in a pre-budget boost to chancellor John Healey, but firms are continuing to cut vacancies.
The latest data on the UK labour market, just released, shows that the UK unemployment rate fell to 4.7% in June to August, down from 4.9% a month ago.
That’s better than expected – City economists had forecast a rise to 5%.
In its final snapshot of Britain’s jobs market ahead of the budget in two week’s time, the Office for National Statistics reports that employment rose, by 102,000 jobs, to 34,577m in the last quarter.
The number of people unemployed fell by 47,000 in the quarter to 1.712m, and there was a small (16,000) drop in the number of people ‘economically inactive’, to 9.091m.
But worryingly, the number of vacancies has seen its largest fall since the start of the year, falling by 21,000 in the last quarter.
That pulled the number of vacancies down to 691,000 in July to September, down from over 1.2m in early 2022. This is the first time the total has been below 700,000 since February to April 2021.
double quotation markThis is mainly from smaller firms, who continue to suggest that they may not be recruiting because of increased labour costs.
That’s a reference to the higher employer National Insurance Contributions (NICs) brought in by Healey’s predecessor, Rachel Reeves, and the rise in the minimum wage, which have made it costlier to hire staff.
7am BST: UK labour market data
10am BST: ZEW index of eurozone economic sentiment
10am BST: Eurozone construction output for August
2.30pm BST: BIST Committee questions Secretary of State Jonathan Reynolds

A mixed picture on wage growth
Regular pay growth rose in the last quarter, today’s labour market report shows.
But once you account for bonuses, wage growth slowed.
The ONS reports that regulator pay grew by 3.7% in the June-August quarter, up from 3.6% a month ago.
But growth in total pay (including bonuses) was 3.7% in June to August 2026, down from 3.9% in May-July.
3m ago07.18 BSTConstruction led fall in vacancies
Vacancies fell particularly sharply across the construction sector, suggesting Britain’s builders cut back on hiring last summer.
Vacancy estimates decreased on the quarter, with early estimates for July to September 2026 suggesting a decrease of 21,000 (2.9%) vacancies to 691,000, compared with April to June 2026; this is the first time the total has been below 700,000 since February to April 2021.
Vacancy estimates decreased in 14 of the 18 industry sectors, compared with April to June 2026; the largest industry decrease was in construction (down 7,000 vacancies).
Vacancy estimates decreased in 4 of the 5 employment size bands, compared with April to June 2026; the largest decrease was for businesses with 1 to 9 employees (down 21,000 vacancies).
